item.title: A relativistic von K\'arm\'an relation for assessing applicability of hydrodynamics
item.description: arXiv:2611.26791v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Relativistic viscous hydrodynamics is a widely used theoretical framework for simulating quark-gluon plasma (QGP) dynamics in relativistic heavy-ion collisions. One open question is how to quantitatively assess the validity of a hydrodynamic description of such a system. In this work, we extract the poles of linear response functions from numerical simulations of hydrodynamics and Boltzmann transport. By comparing these responses as a function of the rescaled wavenumber $\bar{k}$, we identify the wavenumber range over which hydrodynamics captures the underlying microscopic dynamics. We show that the averaged Knudsen number, $\langle\mathrm{Kn}^{*}\rangle$, which we define using the von K\'arm\'an relation, serves as a measure of $\bar{k}$. We find that $\langle\mathrm{Kn}^{*}\rangle_{\rm max}\sim 1$ marks the approximate upper limit of agreement between the linear responses of second-order viscous hydrodynamics and Boltzmann transport.
item.dc:creator: Yuuka Kanakubo, Volker Koch

item.title: Nuclear Shell Model on the Light Front
item.description: arXiv:2611.26895v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Light-front descriptions of nuclear structure provide a relativistic framework that can potentially deepen our understanding of nuclear structure by revealing effects that are absent from traditional non-relativistic treatments. To utilize this framework, we start from the light-front harmonic oscillator to analytically calculate the shell structure and electromagnetic form factors. The relativistic shell model shows that the light-front result recovers the nonrelativistic oscillator limit while introducing shell splitting that depends on the longitudinal excitation quantum number. We derive the resulting effects on the shell model and use the Hellmann-Feynman theorem to identify the longitudinal confinement interaction as the origin of this splitting. We illustrate these results through applications to $^{48}\mathrm{Ca}$ and $^{208}\mathrm{Pb}$. In addition, we demonstrate a substantial difference between form factors calculated using non-relativistic and light-front treatments, a difference that further underscores the importance of including relativistic effects in the description of nuclear structure. Our findings demonstrate a tractable approach to relativistic nuclear calculations and show how extending nuclear models beyond the non-relativistic approximation can yield meaningful physical insight.
item.dc:creator: Zhenkai Fu, Adam Freese, Gerald A. Miller

item.title: u4lib: An AI-Ready Computational Framework for U(4) Symmetry Algebra, Wigner Coupling, and Racah Recoupling Coefficients
item.description: arXiv:2611.27235v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Wigner's supermultiplet symmetry treats nucleon spin and isospin within a common U(4)/SU(4) description. The C++ library u4lib supplies the coupling coefficients and algebraic operations needed for calculations in this scheme. Users can construct irreducible representations (irreps), obtain dimensions and Casimir invariants, conjugate states, enumerate the canonical Gelfand-Tsetlin and physical $\mathrm{SU_S(2)}\otimes\mathrm{SU_T(2)}$ bases with inner multiplicities, and decompose tensor products. Matrix-element routines cover the canonical U(4) generators and the physical spin $\mathbf{S}$, isospin $\mathbf{T}$, and Gamow-Teller-type tensor $\mathbf{U}$. Wigner coupling and Racah recoupling coefficients are evaluated by the 2024 procedure of Dang et al. The implementation builds on u3lib, with a header-only C++ interface and corresponding Python bindings. A catalog of agent skills assists an AI agent in preparing, executing, and checking calculations through natural-language requests.

item.title: Thermal photon production in massless boost-invariant gases: hydrodynamization without thermalization
item.description: arXiv:2611.27332v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study hydrodynamization and thermalization in ultrarelativistic heavy-ion collisions using relativistic kinetic theory. Modelling the quark-gluon plasma as a classical gas of massless particles undergoing a boost-invariant longitudinal expansion, we solve the Boltzmann equation in the relaxation-time approximation via a semi-analytical method based on the method of moments. We show that the energy-momentum tensor is well described by relativistic fluid dynamics even when the system is far from local equilibrium. The single-particle distribution function, on the other hand, is not well approximated by a hydrodynamic truncation, suggesting that the onset of hydrodynamic behaviour does not require thermalization. We then quantify how the departure from equilibrium affects the emission rate of thermal photons in the forward scattering approximation, and show that non-equilibrium corrections beyond the hydrodynamic limit can have a significant impact on this observable.
item.dc:creator: Caio V. P. de Brito, Gabriel S. Denicol

item.title: Nuclear Urca cooling in magnetar crust and anomalous heating
item.description: arXiv:2611.27628v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a new result that the nuclear Urca process in magnetars, associated with ultrastrong magnetic field, dramatically alters the neutrino cooling efficiency to support higher surface temper ature, which is not common in ordinary neutron stars. A new formalism for neutrino luminosity accommodating finite temperature on top of magnetic field is extended with the use of realistic nuclear structure inputs for the Urca pair 29Na-29Mg. We find that the neutrino luminosity of Urca pair shows a spiral variation as a function of magnetic field and crust density, while the Urca pair persists, in contrast to previous studies. Applying geometrically correct volumetric energy loss rate to Urca shell at fixed density with varying magnetic field strength, our results show that thermally populated excited states at finite temperature enhance neutrino luminosity, whereas conditions con strained Urca-pair formation driven by ultrastrong magnetic field reduce cooling efficiency, which can explain high temperature of magnetar surface as a new possibility.
item.dc:creator: LInjing Qi, Qiye Hu, Xinxu Wang, Yudong Luo, Ligang Cao, Longjun Wang, Toshitaka Kajino, Hiroyuki Sagawa, Fengshou Zhang

item.title: Nuclear Precision and Multimessenger Constraints on Neutron-Star Structure
item.description: arXiv:2611.27669v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Neutron-star cores retain structural freedom beyond the constraints supplied by nuclear measurements. We quantify this freedom through an observable-dependent variance ceiling and identify radius--Love compensation as a mechanism suppressing nuclear constraints on tides. Across four data-conditioned equation-of-state families, a pulsar radius measured to 0.3 km paired with a binary tide measured to 10\% removes 44--68\% of the current logarithmic Love-number variance. The framework connects laboratory precision and complementary stellar measurements to core structure.
item.dc:creator: Hisham Anwer, A. Adel, E. Omar

item.title: Soft--hard Bayesian inference in heavy-ion collisions
item.description: arXiv:2611.27971v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bayesian analyses of jet quenching commonly constrain jet--medium interaction parameters using a fixed quark-gluon plasma (QGP) background obtained from a soft-sector calibration. This approach neglects uncertainty in the medium and prevents hard observables from providing additional constraints on its properties. We investigate these effects in Pb--Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=2.76$ TeV using sequential Bayesian inference in a reduced three-parameter space. We vary the initial normalization and nucleon width of the medium together with the jet--medium coupling, combining JETSCAPE medium evolution with MATTER+LBT calculations of high-$p_T$ hadron and inclusive-jet suppression. We first constrain all three parameters using the hard observables alone, then incorporate a projected soft-sector posterior through sequential inference. We find that the hard observables are sensitive to the medium properties and reveal substantial correlations with the jet--medium coupling, reflecting their compensating effects on jet quenching. Propagating the soft-sector information shifts the preferred coupling relative to a fixed-medium extraction, with the update driven primarily by hadron-suppression measurements. Despite substantial differences in the medium parameters and coupling favored by hard-observable-only and sequential inference, their suppression predictions remain similar over much of the measured range. These findings highlight the difficulty of distinguishing changes in the QGP medium from changes in microscopic jet--medium interaction strength using inclusive suppression measurements alone.

item.title: Parity-violating optical rotation in the Th-229 nuclear clock transition
item.description: arXiv:2611.26784v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The exceptionally low-energy nuclear transition in $^{229}$Th provides a new opportunity to study hadronic parity violation (PV) by optical methods. The PV nucleon--nucleus interaction admixes opposite-parity nuclear states into the $5/2^+$ ground state and the $3/2^+$ isomer, thereby inducing an electric-dipole amplitude $E1_{\rm PV}$ that interferes with the magnetic-dipole clock transition amplitude $M1$. In a single-valence-neutron Nilsson model, we find $|E1_{\rm PV}/M1| \sim 2\times10^{-5}$. This interference can be detected as a parity-violating nuclear optical rotation (PVNOR) of resonant laser light transmitted through a $^{229}$Th-doped crystal. For a highly-doped CaF$_2$ crystal fiber, the estimated rotation is of order $10^{-6}\,{\rm rad}$. A crossed-polarizer measurement can reach this sensitivity with existing ultraviolet laser technology. We also analyze systematic effects in the form of optical birefringence, stray magnetic-field-induced Faraday rotation, and local crystal defects. Such a measurement would provide the first direct probe of the PV neutron-nucleus interaction constant, $g_n$.
item.dc:creator: Sebastian Lahs, Thorsten Schumm, Victor V. Flambaum, David DeMille

item.title: Evidence for Y-shaped color confinement of fully heavy baryons
item.description: arXiv:2611.27014v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The geometry of color confinement in baryons remains a fundamental question in quantum chromodynamics. We investigate whether heavy-quark spectroscopy can distinguish a genuine three-body Y-shaped confining interaction from a sum of pairwise $\Delta$-shaped interaction. Using a high-precision three-body Schr\"odinger solver, we perform a simultaneous analysis of experimentally measured bottomonium masses and lattice-QCD calculations of $\Omega_{bbb}$ excitation energies. For each confinement scenario, interaction parameters are independently optimized against the combined spectra. We find that the Y-shaped potential provides a consistent description of both systems, whereas the $\Delta$-shaped potential exhibits significant discrepancies. Our results provide spectroscopic evidence favoring a collective three-body confining interaction and establish triply-heavy baryon spectroscopy as a complementary probe of the nonperturbative geometry of color confinement.
item.dc:creator: Jiaxing Zhao, Shuzhe Shi, Pengfei Zhuang

item.title: Mass Spectra and Radiative Decay Widths of \(D_{s0}^{*}(2317)^+\), \(D_{s1}(2460)^+\) and \(D'_{s1}(2536)^+\)
item.description: arXiv:2611.27363v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Inspired by recent experimental reports on the radiative decay \(D_{s1}(2460)^{+}\to D_s^{*+}\gamma\) and the branching-fraction ratio \(\mathcal{B}[D_{s1}(2460)^{+}\to D_s^{*+}\gamma]/\mathcal{B}[D_{s1}(2460)^{+}\to D_s^{+}\gamma]\), we investigate the mass spectra and radiative decay widths of \(D_{s0}^{*}(2317)^+\), \(D_{s1}(2460)^+\) and \(D_{s1}'(2536)^+\). Within the chiral quark model combined with the Gaussian Expansion Method, the mass spectra obtained agree reasonably well with the experimental data. Besides, the branching-fraction ratio obtained in this work is \(\mathcal{B}[D_{s1}(2460)^{+}\to D_s^{*+}\gamma]/\mathcal{B}[D_{s1}(2460)^{+}\to D_s^{+}\gamma] = 0.57\) and \(\Gamma(D_{s0}^{*}(2317)^{+}\to D_s^{*+}\gamma) = 3.80\,\mathrm{keV}\). By analyzing our theoretical results against the latest experimental measurements, we conclude that the \(D_{s1}(2460)^{+}\) can be treated as a mixed state of \(1^1P_1\) and \(1^3P_1\), and it may contain both the \(c\bar{s}\) component and the tetraquark component. In addition, we also obtain \(\Gamma(D'_{s1}(2536)^{+}\to D_s^{*+}\gamma) = 9.14\,\mathrm{keV}\) and \(\Gamma(D'_{s1}(2536)^{+}\to D_s^{+}\gamma) = 8.59\,\mathrm{keV}\) by treating \(D'_{s1}(2536)^+\) as a meson state. More precise experimental data are required to pin down the internal structure of these states.
item.dc:creator: Shirui Zhao, Yuxuan Du, Manying Pan, Hongxia Huang, Jialun Ping

item.title: Quantum computing for gearing down complex many-fermion problems
item.description: arXiv:2611.27402v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum computing unlocks exciting opportunities to extend first-principles calculations of quantum many-body systems beyond classical computing limits. Despite advances in algorithms and proof-of-principle experiments, large-scale {\it ab initio} calculations on noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices remain challenging. We introduce a quantum-classical framework that identifies compact single-particle bases to bring otherwise intractable many-fermion problems within classical reach while preserving an accurate ground-state description. We develop an efficient adaptive search scheme driven by simulated annealing that jointly optimizes natural-orbital-guided transformations and active-space selections. A quantum-assisted ground-state estimator provides search guidance using low-depth circuits and relaxed accuracy requirements, making the framework promising for NISQ devices. We demonstrate the framework's applicability for the nuclear structure of the oxygen isotopes. Our framework opens a new route to tackling complex {\it ab initio} many-fermion problems across disciplines through quantum-assisted basis reduction.
item.dc:creator: Weijie Du, Filippo Fornetti, James P. Vary

item.title: Neural variational Skyrmions as a topological benchmark: emergent symmetry, precision energies and KAN--MLP comparison
item.description: arXiv:2611.27411v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We propose the three-dimensional Skyrme model as a topological benchmark for neural variational methods and construct fully three-dimensional Skyrmions with baryon number $B=1,\ldots,4$ without imposing a symmetry ansatz, with high precision. For $B=2,3,4$, the relaxation of these Skyrmions starts from $B$ unit-charge lumps with random positions and orientations, which carry no symmetry information. The known toroidal, tetrahedral, and cubic Skyrmions nevertheless emerge spontaneously. The resulting variational energies for $B=1,\ldots,4$ lie slightly below the published reference values. The neural method highlights the high accuracy for retaining the topological charge, differing from $B$ by at most $10^{-6}$ in the highest-precision solutions. Our numerical method goes through physical constraint tests such as the Derrick virial relation and the Faddeev--Bogomolny bound, together with evaluation / verification through independent quadratures and resolution sweeps. We then compare Kolmogorov--Arnold networks (KANs) with multilayer perceptrons (MLPs) in more than a thousand training runs, both with and without a rational-map ansatz. With default settings, KANs appear markedly superior, but most of the gap disappears once the MLP activation function and learning rate are tuned. KANs remain more parameter-efficient and more robust at fixed epoch budget, while MLPs with the tuned activation function perform at least as well at fixed wall-clock time. We also argue that continuous gradient descent cannot smoothly change the topological sector of our neural field, clarifying the origin of topological freezing observed in our neural variational solvers. Our results on the neural methods applied to Skyrmions pave a research ground for AI-agentic benchmarks for classical topological solitons, toward AI-assisted soliton physics.
item.dc:creator: Koji Hashimoto, Masaki Murata, Gakuto Ogiwara

item.title: Uncovering the mechanism of chiral three-nucleon force in driving spin-orbit splitting
item.description: arXiv:2404.02007v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The three-nucleon force (3NF) is crucial in shaping the shell structure of atomic nuclei, particularly impacting the enhancement of spin-orbit (SO) splitting, especially in nuclei with significant deviations from stability. Despite its importance, the specific mechanisms driving this enhancement remain unclear. In this study, we introduce a decomposition scheme based on the rank of irreducible tensors forming the 3NF, derived from chiral effective field theory at next-to-next-to-leading order, to elucidate their influence on SO splitting. Within the shell-model framework, our analysis reveals that the rank-1 component of the 3NF is the primary factor enlarging the energy gap between the $0p_{3/2}$ and $0p_{1/2}$ single-particle levels in $p$-shell nuclei. Since the rank-1 component originates exclusively from the $2\pi$-exchange 3NF, our finding will not depend on the choice of the low-energy constants of contact terms. We also remark on the antisymmetry of the rank-1 3NF, which can affect the quantum entanglement of spin states. This study lays the groundwork for further exploration into this field toward a microscopic understanding of the 3NF impact on the nuclear shell structure.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Phys. Lett. B 855, 138839 (2024); Corrigendum: Phys. Lett. B 883, 141166 (2026)
item.dc:creator: Tokuro Fukui, Giovanni De Gregorio, Angela Gargano

item.title: Nuclear pasta in hot neutron-star matter and proto-neutron stars
item.description: arXiv:2603.16220v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate nuclear pasta phases appearing in hot neutron-star matter based on the compressible liquid-drop model, where the matter consists of a dense liquid phase and a dilute gas phase separated by a sharp interface.The surface tension is calculated self-consistently from the Thomas-Fermi approximation, and it depends on temperature and isospin asymmetry. We employ relativistic mean-field (RMF) models with different symmetry energy slopes to describe nuclear interactions. It is found that the RMF models with smaller symmetry energy slopes result in various pasta phases at low temperatures, whereas those with larger symmetry energy slopes yield only the droplet configuration up to the crust-core transition density. We examine the occurrence and influence of pasta phases in proto-neutron stars with a constant entropy per baryon. These pasta phases may occur in the inner crust and play an important role in the thermal evolution of the star.
item.dc:creator: Jian Zhou, Junbo Pang, Hong Shen, Jinniu Hu

item.title: Anisotropic Coulomb Interaction in Strongly Magnetized Electron Gas at Zero Temperature in Relativistic Quantum Framework
item.description: arXiv:2611.25688v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a microscopic derivation of Debye screening in a Landau-quantized electron gas subject to a strong magnetic field. By calculating the photon self-energy within the RPA framework, we explore how Landau levels influence the screening properties of the electron gas. Due to the quantum periodicity of Landau levels, the screening behavior is relatively insensitive to variations in the carrier density within each occupation cycle compared to the drastic changes induced by the magnetic field strength. Within a single occupation cycle, the Kohn anomaly dominates the low-density regime; at higher densities, its characteristic momentum shifts into the asymptotic high-momentum regime, rendering its singular contribution less prominent over the active screening domain and allowinga smooth orientation-dependent anisotropy to govern the system. Furthermore, a subtle competition in directional screening is observed between the parallel and perpendicular directions to the field depending on the density domain. At lower field strengths, multiple quantum oscillations emerge from the simultaneous participation of various Landau levels, marking a qualitative transition toward the isotropic three-dimensional limit. Our findings reveal anisotropic screening effects and provide insights into the behavior of charged impurities in such systems.
item.dc:creator: Tomoyuki Maruyama, A. Baha Balantekin, Myung-Ki Cheoun, Toshitaka Kajino, Eunseok Whang

item.title: Testable leptogenesis and $0\nu\beta\beta$ decay in extended seesaw model
item.description:
arXiv:2410.12180v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate the possibility of observable neutrinoless double beta decay $( 0 
u  eta eta)$ and viable leptogenesis within a low-scale extended inverse seesaw mechanism with additional sterile neutrinos. General effective field theory (EFT) considerations suggest that if there are experimentally observable signatures in $0 
u  eta  eta$-decay and a lepton asymmetry generated by heavy right-handed neutrino decays, thermal leptogenesis is likely to be unviable. However, in this work, we show that in the context of low-scale leptogenesis, one can obtain the observed baryon asymmetry of the universe and observable signatures of $0 
u  eta  eta$ decay in the presence of additional sterile neutrinos. In this framework, the light neutrino masses are suppressed by the extended seesaw parameter, $\mu$, thereby allowing for $\mathcal{O}(10\, \mathrm{TeV})$ right-handed (RH) neutrinos, while avoiding small Yukawa couplings as in other neutrino mass models and near degeneracies in the RH neutrino spectrum as required by the low-scale leptogenesis paradigm. Contributions to the $0 
u  eta  eta$-decay rate from additional sterile neutrinos can be appreciable, while the corresponding contributions to the early universe lepton asymmetry washout rate are suppressed by other parameters not entering the $0 
u  eta  eta$-decay amplitudes. We show that for keV-MeV scale, sterile neutrinos future ton-scale $0
u eta eta$-decay experiments offer potential signals while maintaining viable leptogenesis.
item.dc:creator: Gang Li, Michael J. Ramsey-Musolf, Supriya Senapati, Sebasti\'an Urrutia Quiroga

item.title: Lattice QCD determination of the $\gamma Z$ box contribution to the proton weak charge
item.description: arXiv:2601.06582v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present the first lattice QCD determination of the $\gamma Z$ box contribution to parity-violating electron-proton scattering, $\square_{\gamma Z}$, a key ingredient for the precise tests of the Standard Model via the proton weak charge. Our calculation covers the electron beam energies up to $E=155$ MeV. At $E=0$, the vector contribution is known analytically and excluded by convention; for the remaining axial-vector component we obtain $\square_{\gamma Z}(0)=0.00411(9)$. Incorporating this result implies a value for weak charge of $Q_W^p=0.06987(50)$. The calculated energy dependence of $\square_{\gamma Z}$ is directly relevant to the upcoming P2 experiment at Mainz, which will operate at the optimized beam energy of 155 MeV to extract $Q_W^p$.Although the systematic error budget in this exploratory study is not yet complete, this work establishes a lattice-QCD framework for computing the $\gamma Z$ box contribution and demonstrates the feasibility of a first-principles approach, providing a foundation for future calculations with improved systematic control.
item.dc:creator: Zhao-long Zhang, Xu Feng, Mikhail Gorchtein, Lu-Chang Jin, Chuan Liu, Chien-Yeah Seng

item.title: Probing gluon saturation through inclusive hadron production in DIS
item.description: arXiv:2609.15461v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate gluon saturation effects in semi-inclusive deep inelastic scattering (SIDIS) at small-$x$ within the Color Glass Condensate framework. We compute the SIDIS cross section at leading order in the dipole picture, expressing it in terms of the dipole-target scattering amplitude. We validate our framework by comparing with the charged hadron spectra measured at HERA. Our predictions for the EIC indicate that saturation effects result in significant nuclear suppression in the SIDIS cross section, and can provide complementary constraints on the initial condition for the Balitsky-Kovchegov evolution extracted from inclusive DIS data. These results demonstrate that SIDIS measurements at the EIC are sensitive to nonlinear QCD dynamics in the saturation regime.
item.dc:creator: Carlisle Casuga, Swaleha Mulani, Heikki M\"antysaari
